hints: Start from the defining equation for each quantity: $F = ma$ for force, $p = mv$ for momentum, $p = F/A$ for pressure, and $W = Fs$ for work.
Recall that force in base units is $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, so for pressure you must divide this by area in $\text{m}^{2}$ and check the power of $\text{m}$ carefully.
Work out $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ divided by $\text{m}^{2}$ and compare its $\text{m}$ power with the $\text{m}^{-2}$ shown for pressure.
walkthrough: Write each derived unit from its defining equation using SI base units $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$.
Force: $F = ma$ gives $\text{kg} \times \text{m s}^{-2} = \text{kg m s}^{-2}$, which matches the given unit.
Momentum: $p = mv$ gives $\text{kg} \times \text{m s}^{-1} = \text{kg m s}^{-1}$, which matches the given unit.
Work: $W = Fs$ gives $\text{kg m s}^{-2} \times \text{m} = \text{kg m}^{2} \text{s}^{-2}$, which matches the given unit.

Pressure: $p = F/A$ gives $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ divided by $\text{m}^{2}$, which is $\text{kg m}^{-1} \text{s}^{-2}$. The stated $\text{kg m}^{-2} \text{s}^{-2}$ has an extra $\text{m}^{-1}$ and is wrong. This is option C

options.A: From $F = ma$, the newton is $\text{kg} \times \text{m s}^{-2} = \text{kg m s}^{-2}$, so this is correct.
options.B: From $p = mv$, momentum is $\text{kg} \times \text{m s}^{-1} = \text{kg m s}^{-1}$, so this is correct.
options.C: Pressure is force divided by area, giving $\text{kg m}^{-1} \text{s}^{-2}$, not $\text{kg m}^{-2} \text{s}^{-2}$, so this is not correct.
options.D: From $W = Fs$, work is $\text{kg m s}^{-2} \times \text{m} = \text{kg m}^{2} \text{s}^{-2}$, so this is correct.
